## Plan

### 1. Move the fixtures path to where the whole suite shares things

Goal: let a new test file reach `tests/fixtures/` without importing it from a module about harness recordings.

Criterion: every reference to the `FIXTURES` constant. It lives in `tests/recordings.py` today, which is "the streams recorded from a real harness, and the feed they render as". The goldens phase 7 adds are prompts, not recordings, so the path moves to `tests/conftest.py`, "what the whole suite shares", and every importer follows.

Behaviour-preserving: nothing under `src/` changes.

### 2. Give the state directory a home for worktrees and sessions

Goal: name the two directories under `.dreamcatcher/` that a session's files live in, so nothing else has to spell the layout out.

Criterion: every path that `design.md`'s "The state directory" section names and the code has no property for yet, leaving the ones a later phase writes. That is `worktrees/` and `sessions/`.

### 3. Choose the harness that a label's dispatch runs on

Goal: answer the question `design.md`'s Configuration section poses, which phase 2 left to the phase that dispatches. A label carrying a block for the harness the run named runs on that one, and a label with no block for it runs on the harness it does carry.

Criterion: the rule belongs on `DispatchMapping` in `config.py`, beside the blocks it reads. Cover both arms.

### 4. Turn a harness into the adapter that runs it

Goal: give the one place that knows every harness's adapter a home, so nothing else has to know how many harnesses there are.

Criterion: a lookup from every `Harness` member to its adapter, in a module of its own, since `adapters.py` cannot import the adapters that import it. A test asserts the lookup covers the enum, so a harness added later without an adapter fails there rather than in a round.

### 5. Compose the first round's prompt

Goal: render a label's template with the issue's number, and end it with the postscript that asks the session to mark every post it makes on GitHub.

Criterion: the marker and the prose that carries it, per `design.md`'s "The relay". `{issue}` is the only substitution the dispatcher owns, so the render replaces that literal and nothing else. A golden file per harness holds the whole composed prompt, under `tests/fixtures/prompts/`, so the reviewer reads what the agent will read.

### 6. Cut a session for a dispatched issue

Goal: produce everything a dispatch produces: the session key, the branch, the worktree nested under `.dreamcatcher/worktrees/`, and `session.json`.

Criterion: `design.md`'s "Sessions, worktrees, branches" names each part. The session is cut from an up-to-date `origin/main`, so the creation fetches first. A creation that fails after git has made the worktree takes the worktree and the branch away again, and reports the failure that started the back-out rather than any failure the back-out hits.

Tests cut a real worktree in a real checkout with a real origin, read `session.json` back through its model, and prove that a failed creation leaves no worktree and no branch.

> written by an agent

## Coherence review

> `src/dreamcatcher/sessions.py:66-68` and `94-105`: the "leaves nothing behind" guarantee is not what the code establishes. `create()`'s docstring states: "Should writing the record then fail, the worktree and the branch go away again, so a failed creation leaves nothing behind". But `_back_out()` (lines 94-105) only removes the git worktree and the branch. It never touches `state.sessions / key`, the directory that `write_json`'s `_write()` creates via `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` before it opens the file to write.

Accepted. The docstring now says the worktree and the branch go away and claims nothing wider. I left the empty session directory where it falls rather than sweeping it: nothing reads a session directory to decide anything, since the tick reconciles by worktree, and cleanup code for a disk-full case is the addition this phase's plan defers.

> The postscript text is committed a second and third time in the golden fixtures. `src/dreamcatcher/prompts.py:17-26` defines `POSTSCRIPT` ... `tests/fixtures/prompts/claude.txt:3-10` and `tests/fixtures/prompts/codex.txt:3-10` each hard-code that exact same eight-line text verbatim ... here the "golden" is just a second (and third) copy of a literal already defined once in source.

Accepted, though not by the fix the finding proposed, which would have left the golden holding only the template and so a third copy of that. Both fixture files are gone. The test now composes each harness's template and asserts the result equals the rendered opening plus `POSTSCRIPT`, read from its one home, so a new harness with no opening still fails the test. `tests/fixtures/prompts/` was the only reason `FIXTURES` moved to `conftest.py`, so that move is reverted too and those four test files leave the diff. The composed prompt is in this PR's description instead, which is where a reviewer of this phase will read it.

> `choose_harness` sits in the config-parsing module, which the plan itself says should only parse ... `specs/2026-08-17-skeleton/plan.md:311-312` states the intended boundary explicitly: "Phase 2 parses the blocks and leaves the choice to the phase that dispatches".

Rejected. That sentence says which phase makes the choice, not which module holds it, and `design.md` puts the rule itself under Configuration: "There is no separate pin: what the repo agrees about a label is already in which blocks it wrote." The rule reads nothing but the mapping's own blocks, so asking the mapping is the reading with no feature envy in it, and the proposed inline expression would put `harness_settings`'s internals in `sessions.py`.

> `Launch` and `Session` model the same "fixed session identity" concept twice ... delete `Launch` from `src/dreamcatcher/adapters.py:20-31` entirely and change `Adapter.first_round`/`Adapter.resume` to take the `Session`.

Rejected. `Launch` is what one round starts with, and its prompt is that round's own, which a resume round's is not. Handing an adapter the whole dispatch record would give it the issue, the label, the branch and the worktree as well, and `design.md` keeps that boundary at "a small frozen object" on purpose.

> `sessions.create` breaks with the vocabulary this same diff establishes for the operation ... rename `create` to `cut`.

Accepted in part. The prose moved to the name rather than the other way round: the module and the function now open with "Create a session", and "cut" is left where a worktree or a branch is the thing being cut, which is what git does. The plan calls this "session creation", and `sessions.create` says that in one word.

> `Session.key` and `Launch.session` name the identical value with two different words ... rename `Launch.session` (`adapters.py:28`) to `Launch.key`.

Rejected. `launch.session` reads as the session that this launch belongs to, and `session.key` as the key that names it, so the phase 8 call site says `Launch(session=session.key, ...)` and means it. `launch.key` would read as the launch's own key, which there is no such thing as.

The root cause, same edit, deep modules, defensive code, cross-site rules and one model lenses returned nothing else.

> written by an agent

## Code review

> `src/dreamcatcher/sessions.py:84-85` — `add_worktree` sits outside the try/except that triggers `_back_out`, but git does not fail atomically. I verified with a live git repo that `git worktree add -b <branch> <path> <start>` creates the branch *before* validating/populating the destination, so a failure partway ... still leaves the branch behind while the command exits non-zero.

Accepted. I reproduced it too: git prints "Preparing worktree (new branch 'probe')", makes the branch, then fails on the destination. The add now runs inside the try, so the back-out reaches what git left. A new test occupies the worktree's place, drives the failure, and asserts no branch survives; it fails when the add is moved back out, so it pins the fix. That test also runs `remove_worktree` against a directory that is not a worktree, so the first `suppress(CommandError)` now catches something.

> `src/dreamcatcher/sessions.py:40-48` — `Session.key: str` is stored in `session.json`, but design.md's ... sections enumerate that file's fields explicitly: "`session.json` (issue, label, branch, worktree path, harness, model, effort, rendered first prompt — frozen at dispatch)" — no `key`. The key is already carried by the record's own path.

Accepted. The field is gone. `Session.key` is now a property reading the worktree's own directory name, so the key still reads as one word at a call site and the record stores it once, in the path that the key names.

> `_back_out`'s exception-suppression is never actually triggered ... If `suppress(CommandError)` were deleted and `remove_worktree`/`delete_branch` called bare, this test would still pass unchanged.

Accepted, and fixed by the same test as the first finding.

> `test_a_session_cuts_a_branch_of_its_own_from_origins_main_as_it_is_now` only deletes and lets `create()` recreate the local `refs/remotes/origin/main` ref — it never pushes a new commit to `upstream` after cloning, so it cannot distinguish "fetches origin's main" from "fetches origin's main as it currently is".

Accepted. The test now commits to main, pushes it, and winds the checkout's tracking ref back to what it knew before, so only a fetch of the creation's own brings the newer main. It asserts the new file is in the worktree, and it fails when the fetch is taken out.

> `src/dreamcatcher/config.py:51-61` — `choose_harness` docstring states a guarantee that depends on an invariant it never names ... that's only true because `Harness` currently has exactly two members.

Accepted. The docstring now says there are two harnesses, which is what makes the one remaining block the only one.

> `src/dreamcatcher/config.py:51-61` (`choose_harness`) — phase 8's planned startup check won't cover every harness a tick can actually dispatch to ... a repo whose config mixes single-harness labels will dispatch a session onto a harness that was never checked for its CLI at startup.

Deferred. The check is phase 8's to write and does not exist yet, so this is a note for the phase that builds it rather than a change here; I will file it as an issue.

> `src/dreamcatcher/sessions.py:41` — `Session.issue: int` has no lower-bound constraint, unlike its config siblings ... worth a `PositiveInt`.

Rejected. The issue number arrives from GitHub's own listing, so the boundary that could ever see a bad one is `github.Issue`, not a record written from it. A second check here is the guard at the wrong layer.

> **tests/test_sessions.py:34-37** — `written()` reimplements the `Model.model_validate_json(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))` idiom that already exists twice ... A shared `read_json(model, path)` helper in tests/conftest.py would let all three call one line.

Rejected. It is one line at each of three sites, and a shared helper for it would hide nothing.

> **tests/test_sessions.py:36** — `record = state.sessions / KEY / "session.json"` hardcodes the literal `"session.json"` instead of importing `RECORD`.

Rejected. The file's name is an interface: `scry` and a person both go looking for `session.json`. A test that took the name from the code it tests would pass through a rename that broke both.

> `_back_out` suppresses both git failures with no logging ... the caller of `create()` sees only the original `ReportableError`, with no indication that cleanup also failed.

Rejected for this phase. There is no log and no tick record to say it in yet, and a worktree that will not go away is what the tick's reconciliation reads in phase 8.

> `codex.py:96`'s `-c` overrides interpolate config values into a quoted string without escaping.

Rejected. The file is unchanged here, and whoever writes `dreamcatcher.toml` already writes the whole prompt, which is a larger lever than one `-c` flag.

The correctness, cross-platform and altitude lenses found nothing else, and the reader's-context lens passed the postscript as an instruction the agent can follow without outside knowledge.

> written by an agent

## Simplification opportunities

1. **Drop the back-out, and let the tick sweep instead.** This would remove `_back_out`, the try/except in `create`, the `CommandError` import, and the two tests that drive a failed creation — and with them the whole "git makes the branch before it fails" reasoning that this PR had to establish. Phase 8 already enumerates session worktrees every tick, so it could remove any worktree with no `session.json` beside it, which is a sweep it would want anyway for a daemon killed mid-dispatch. What the PR gives up: a failed creation leaves a worktree and a branch lying about until the next tick, and phase 8 grows a sweep its plan does not currently name.

2. **Drop `session.json`, and read the config each round.** Almost every field derives from the key and the label's config block, so `Session`, `write_json`, `RECORD`, and the tests that read the record back would all go, leaving `create` to cut a worktree and return a key. What the PR gives up: the requirements brief's "a session keeps the harness, model, and effort it was dispatched with, even if I edit the config mid-flight". Editing the config would reach every session in flight, and a label removed from the config mid-session would leave that session with nothing to resume on.

3. **Drop the harness choice, and always run the harness the run named.** `choose_harness` and its two tests would go, and so would the config's whole single-block case. What the PR gives up: the requirement that some labels go to Claude Code and some to Codex within one process. Each harness would need its own `run`, on its own labels.

4. **Drop the fetch.** One call and one test. What the PR gives up: a session branches from whatever `origin/main` the checkout last heard about, so a long-idle daemon cuts sessions from a stale main and every pull request opens with a diff against old code.

5. **Drop `harnesses.py`.** Nothing in this PR consumes `ADAPTERS`; phase 8 is the caller. The lookup could arrive with that caller instead. What the PR gives up: nothing this phase can demonstrate, which is the point — it is here because the plan asked phase 7 for it.

6. **Drop the `key` property.** Callers would write `session.worktree.name`. What the PR gives up: the word "key" at the call sites that phase 8 will write, for four lines.

After merge, when you run collect, if you raise any new issues, please think about whether they need to be addressed before other existing issues. If so, please mark that issue as blocked by it. (And please add an AGENTS.md rule for this, so I don't have to keep reminding.)

Acted on all of it. The renames and the reworded prose have their own replies inline. Here is the rest.

## The spec now says what the code does

I went back through the phase against both spec documents. Three places had drifted, and the branch corrects them.

`design.md`, "Sessions, worktrees, branches", said "One invariant is checked at dispatch, not assumed: the worktree path is strictly under `.dreamcatcher/worktrees/`." The code carries that by construction instead, so the design now says so: the dispatch builds the path from the state directory and the session key and takes none from a caller, so no check has to say it.

The same section said nothing about the fetch, or about what a failed creation leaves. Both are decisions this phase made, so both are written down now: the dispatch fetches origin's main before it cuts the branch, and a creation that fails from the worktree onwards takes the worktree and the branch away again, because git names the branch before it reaches the worktree.

`plan.md`, phase 7, asked for "the path invariant checked at dispatch", for a failed creation to leave "no trace", and for "golden tests per harness". The first is gone for the reason above. The second now says no worktree and no branch, which is what the back-out reaches. The third now says the prompt each harness's template composes to is pinned in full, which is what the tests do against the one `POSTSCRIPT` constant.

## Three rules in AGENTS.md

Descriptive names, under the other naming rules: name a class or a function that a module exports so that it still says what it is when another module imports it bare.

Keeping the spec true, in the Specs section. It used to say to declare a divergence in the PR. It now says to correct the spec in the same PR so it keeps saying what the code really does, and to say in the PR what you changed and why, so the reviewer reads the divergence rather than finding it.

Blocking order when filing issues, under the conventions: ask of every issue you file whether an issue that is already open has to wait for it, and mark that issue as blocked by the new one when it does. It names GitHub's dependencies API and the trap that the payload wants the blocking issue's API id rather than its number.

## Collect

- #55 — The startup harness check misses a harness a single-block label runs on. `documentation`. This is the note I left in the code review: `plan.md`'s phase 8 scope says the check asks after "the harness it was given", but a label carrying one harness block runs on that harness whatever the run named, so a mixed config dispatches to a CLI nothing looked for. It corrects the plan, not the code.
- #56 — Names that a module exports read as nothing when imported bare. `maintenance`. The sweep that #52's new `AGENTS.md` rule asks for, over `commands.run`, `commands.spawn`, `commands.locate`, `lock.hold`, `clock.now`, `git.fetch` and most of `github.py`.

#13, phase 8, is now marked blocked by #55. Phase 8 is the session that writes that check, so correcting the plan first costs one small change, and correcting it afterwards means the narrow check gets written and then rewritten.

#56 blocks nothing. Phase 8 will follow the rule as written, so it does not have to wait, and doing the sweep later moves a few more call sites, which is mechanical either way. It says to do itself alongside #51, which is the same sweep under the sibling rule over the same files.

Two things I decided not to file. A record write that fails after `documents._write` has made the session directory leaves that directory behind: the spec now says a failed creation leaves no worktree and no branch, which is what the back-out reaches, and nothing reads a session directory to decide anything. And `codex.py` building `model_reasoning_effort="<effort>"` without escaping the value: the tool passes model and effort through to the harness on purpose and never validates either, so a quote in one is a config mistake that the harness reports, not a fault in the tool.
